text.p: German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG said on Monday it would compensate subscribers to its online and Internet access service T-Online with two free hours of service following software troubles.

The company said in a statement that it had solved a number of problems related to the introduction of a new version of the software customers use to connect to the service and to the Internet and that all customers would receive the compensation.
With introduction of the new software, T-Online subscribers often were unable to dial into the service in July and at the beginning of August, but Telekom said the problems have been resolved.
T-Online has around 1.6 million customers. The two free hours of online usage time will be credited to October bills, Telekom said.
